variants.name: Jinja2 Environment with a loader and autoescaping
variants.implementation_notes: Jinja2 is the framework-independent default: build one Environment with a loader (FileSystemLoader/PackageLoader) and autoescape=select_autoescape(['html', 'htm', 'xml']), then env.get_template('orders.html').render(**model). Markers are {{ value }} with {% %} statements, and {% extends %}/{% block %}/{% include %} supply the layout chrome; Flask and FastAPI wire the same object through their templating integrations.
pitfalls: A bare Environment has autoescape=False: without select_autoescape or autoescape=True every {{ value }} is an injection point.
The Environment and its template cache are meant to be created once; building one per request recompiles templates and defeats the cache.
Markup/|safe values opt out of escaping and are sticky in expressions; audit each one rather than sprinkling them for formatting.

variants.name: Django template language through the Django backend
variants.implementation_notes: Inside Django the shipped engine is the Django template language, configured by the TEMPLATES setting with APP_DIRS loaders: the view calls render(request, 'orders.html', {'rows': rows}) and the template uses {{ }} / {% %} with {% extends %} layouts, {% include %} partials and autoescaping on by default for HTML. Choose it over Jinja2 when the project is Django, because contrib apps ship DTL templates and the template-tag ecosystem follows it.
pitfalls: QuerySets are lazy: iterating a manager or touching a related field per row turns one page into N+1 queries, so resolve the model in the view.
Template variable resolution reaches any attribute or zero-argument method of the objects you pass; hand over narrow view models, not domain entities.
autoescape can be switched off per block ({% autoescape off %}) or per value (|safe); both are injection decisions, not formatting conveniences.
